card.title: Director of Warehouse Operations
card.description:
**Director of Warehouse Operations**

**Your Leadership. Our Foundation.**

At **Cash Depot**, you’re not just joining a company, you’re becoming part of a family.

As a nationwide leader in ATM management and financial transaction processing, we’ve built our reputation on innovation, exceptional customer service, and strong partnerships. As we continue expanding our footprint and evolving our solutions, we’re seeking a strategic, hands-on operations leader to oversee the teams that keep our ATM equipment and components ready to support our customers.

When you join Cash Depot, you’re stepping into an organization where your ideas matter, your leadership is valued, and your impact is visible across the business. This is an opportunity to lead four teams, improve how our operations run, and build a high-performing warehouse organization focused on efficiency, quality, and long-term success.

**What We Offer**

* Competitive compensation package
* **Profit Sharing Bonus Program**
* **Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision benefits**
* **Company-paid Life Insurance**
* **Company-paid Short-Term Disability (STD)**
* 401(k) with company match
* Paid time off and holidays
* Monday through Friday daytime schedule
* Leadership visibility with a direct reporting line to the COO
* Opportunity to shape how our operations grow and improve
* Stable, growing organization with nationwide operations

**Position Summary**

The **Director of Warehouse Operations** provides strategic leadership, direction, and oversight for Cash Depot’s Inventory and Warehousing, ATM Parts Repair, ATM Set-Up and Refurbishment, and Purchasing departments.

Reporting directly to the Chief Operating Officer, the Director is accountable for operational efficiency, inventory accuracy, cost management, quality control, productivity, and the timely availability of ATM equipment and components to support company operations and customer commitments.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Operational Leadership & Cost Management**

* Manage departmental budgets and identify opportunities to reduce operating costs.
* Improve productivity and eliminate inefficiencies across warehouse, repair, refurbishment, and purchasing functions.
* Analyze operational data to identify bottlenecks and opportunities for improvement.
* Increase throughput, quality, and profitability across all areas of responsibility.

**Inventory, Repair & Equipment Readiness**

* Improve inventory accuracy, availability, and inventory turns.
* Improve repair turnaround times and reduce replacement costs.
* Ensure ATM equipment is set up, refurbished, and deployment-ready on schedule.
* Maintain quality standards that support company operations and customer commitments.

**Purchasing & Vendor Management**

* Improve vendor pricing, procurement efficiency, and cost controls.
* Ensure timely availability of ATM equipment, parts, and components.
* Build productive vendor relationships that support quality and reliability.

**Team Development & Accountability**

* Lead, develop, and hold accountable four department leaders: the Warehouse Manager, Purchasing Manager, Parts Repair Lead, and Setup/Refurb Lead.
* Set clear performance standards and expectations across all four departments.
* Build and foster high-performing teams aligned with Cash Depot’s culture and values.
* Operate within corporate policy guidelines and business practices.

**Requirements**

* 3–5 years of operations management experience preferred.
* Demonstrated ability to analyze data and identify operational bottlenecks or opportunities.
* Deep understanding of service delivery principles and customer satisfaction.
* Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite or other relevant systems.

**Skills & Qualifications**

* Strong ability to lead and inspire teams.
* Excellent communication skills to collaborate with teams, customers, and leadership.
* Results-oriented with a demonstrated sense of urgency.
* Strong problem-solving, communication, and teamwork skills.
* Ability to adapt to change in the workplace or in assigned duties.
* Ability to balance strategic thinking with hands-on execution.

**Why Cash Depot?**

This is an opportunity to join a growing national organization in a highly visible leadership role. As Director of Warehouse Operations, you’ll lead the teams that keep Cash Depot’s ATM equipment moving, shape how our operations run, and directly influence the service we deliver to customers across the country.

**Join Cash Depot and lead the operations that power our next chapter of growth.**

card.title: Director, Commercialization Partnerships Operations
card.description:
Revolution Medicines is a global, commercial-state oncology company dedicated to discovering, developing and delivering innovative medicines for patients with RAS-addicted cancers. Leveraging its differentiated RAS(ON) tri-complex inhibitor platform, the company is advancing a broad, integrated portfolio of oral RAS(ON) inhibitors designed to directly target the active, cancer-driving state of RAS. Founded on rigorous scientific inquiry and a willingness to challenge long-held assumptions, Revolution Medicines is committed to changing the trajectory of disease for patients with RAS-addicted cancers worldwide.

Our people are united by a shared way of working: follow the science, challenge assumptions, act with urgency and hold ourselves to a high standard of rigor—all in service of patients.

**The Opportunity:**

The Director, Commercialization Partnerships and Operationsserves as the primary operational and partnership role at RevMed headquarters supporting the Senior Director, Commercialization Partnerships and Operations This role is responsible for driving operational and partnership excellence, governance structure, financial tracking, and cross-functional alignment across select regional commercialization partners and territory-specific distributors. This role will also partner with regional commercial heads to support relationship management and commercial readiness across the same distribution partner(s).

By serving as the central HQ liaison, this role ensures seamless coordination between RevMed’s internal functional teams (Supply Chain, Regulatory, Quality, Medical Affairs, Finance) and external partners including regional commercial and distribution partners to achieve commercial readiness, regulatory/MAA approval, compliant named-patient access programs, and reliable product supply for a select region.

Core Responsibilities & Scope:

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) & Governance Framework

* Consistent KPI Architecture**:** Establish, standardize, and monitor a unified commercial and operational KPI framework across select region/partner.
* Commercial & Non-Commercial KPIs: Forecast/order accuracy, market access, medical information metrics, performance to volume targets, order-to-cash cycle times, stockout frequency, inventory buffer levels, and lead-time adherence.
* Regulatory & Quality KPIs*:* Variances/amendment submission timelines, adherence to quality and PV agreements.
* Governance & Decision-Making: Operationalize joint governance bodies (e.g., Joint Steering Committees [JSC], Joint Commercial Committees [JCC], and Joint Operations Committees [JOC]) and joint pricing decisions.
* Define escalation pathways, charter guidelines, voting rights, and decision-making matrices (RevMed vs. Partner/Distributor) across commercial, pricing, regulatory, and supply chain domains.

Financial Reporting & Revenue Reconciliation

* Quarterly Financial Tracking: Partner with RevMed HQ Finance and Partner Commercial Operations to track, report, and analyze quarterly commercial revenue, transfer pricing, and royalty/profit-share milestones. Reconcile financial tracking on quarterly basis as necessary.
* KPI-Based Financial Reconciliation: Lead the quarterly financial reconciliation process across partners based on contracted KPIs, volume tiers, milestone achievements, and operational claw backs or bonuses.
* Commercial Dashboard Management: Maintain real-time executive dashboards reporting financial performance, sales volume, inventory valuation, and partner margin compliance.

**Required Skills, Experience and Education:**

* Education: B.S./B.A. in Business, Life Sciences, Supply Chain, or Finance (MBA or advanced degree preferred).
* Experience: 8–12+ years of experience in the biopharmaceutical industry, with direct experience in Alliance Management, Commercial Operations, Strategic Account Operations, or Global Program Management.
* Cross-Functional Expertise: Proven track record bridging commercial activities with technical/operations functions (Supply Chain, Quality/CMC, Regulatory, Medical Affairs, Finance).
* Negotiation Experience: Demonstrated success developing, negotiating, and operationalizing licensing, distribution, commercialization or alliance agreements.
* Geographic & Regional Knowledge**:** Solid understanding of regional pharmaceutical markets, regulatory environments (regional & national competent authorities), pricing & reimbursement dynamics, and distribution models (direct vs. distributor/partner).
* Travel: Ability to travel up to 30%. Hybrid role, at minimum 2-3 days in office at Redwood City headquarters.

**Preferred Skills:**

* Oncology development, supply chain, and commercialization experience.
* Prior experience in a smaller, rapidly growing biotech or pharmaceutical company.

#LI-JW1 #LI-Remote

The base pay salary range for this full-time position for candidates working onsite at our headquarters in Redwood City, CA is listed below. The range displayed on each job posting is intended to be the base pay salary range for an individual working onsite in Redwood City and will be adjusted for the local market a candidate is based in. Our base pay salary ranges are determined by role, level, and location. Individual base pay salary is determined by multiple factors, including job-related skills, experience, market dynamics, and relevant education or training.

Please note that base pay salary range is one part of the overall total rewards program at RevMed, which includes competitive cash compensation, robust equity awards, strong benefits, and significant learning and development opportunities.

Revolution Medicines is an equal opportunity employer and prohibits unlawful discrimination based on race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity/expression, national origin/ancestry, age, disability, marital status, medical condition, and veteran status.

Revolution Medicines takes protection and security of personal data very seriously and respects your right to privacy while using our website and when contacting us by email or phone. We will only collect, process and use any personal data that you provide to us in accordance with our CCPA Notice and Privacy Policy. For additional information, please contact privacy@revmed.com.

Base Pay Salary Range

$201,000 - $251,000 USD

*We are aware of recent recruitment scams in which individuals or organizations falsely represent themselves as being affiliated with Revolution Medicines. These scams may appear as false job advertisements or unsolicited contacts through communication or chat platforms, email, phone, or text message.*
 
 
*Please note that Revolution Medicines does not extend unsolicited employment offers and will never ask candidates to provide financial information, purchase equipment, or pay fees as part of the hiring process. All legitimate communication from Revolution Medicines will come from an official* ***@revmed.com*** *email address.*
 
 
*If you believe you’ve been contacted by someone impersonating a Revolution Medicines recruiter, please report it to* ***careers@revmed.com*** *so we can share these impersonations with our IT team for tracking and awareness.*

card.title: Director, Facility Operations
card.description:
**Director, Facility Operations** 
The 3-time WNBA Champions Los Angeles Sparks are seeking an innovative, strategic, and revenue-driven **Director, Facility Operations**. This executive will be responsible for working with both in-house employees and 3rd party vendors, and will oversee the day-to-day upkeep and operation of the Los Angeles Sparks’ Training Facility.

**PRINCIPAL DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES**

* Oversee the operation of building systems and equipment, including mechanical, electrical, plumbing, hydro, and food service equipment and direct the work of personnel associated with the systems and building engineering.
* Serve at the primary point of contact for building maintenance, repairs, and facilities-related service requests across all organizational spaces, including offices and venues.
* Assist in the development and implementation of a computerized work order management system to enable occupants to submit service requests, track progress, and support the prioritization and scheduling of maintenance and repair activities.
* Serve as point of contact for local utilities (ex. Southern California Edison for building power).
* Serve as the primary building point of contact for the Fire Marshal, coordinate and attend required inspections, maintain all necessary fire and life safety records and documentation, and schedule and oversee required annual, quarterly, and other periodic testing of building safety systems in accordance with applicable codes and jurisdictional requirements.
* Build and maintain budgets for annual preventative maintenance costs.
* Develop and maintain appropriate inventory levels of supplies, materials, and repair parts based on facility and venue needs, ensuring materials are readily available to support maintenance and repair activities, and maintain accurate inventory records.
* Develop and oversee annual and preventive maintenance schedules for all facilities and building systems; establish and maintain standard operating procedures (SOPs) for facility operations, maintenance, and emergency response; and identify, engage, and manage third-party vendors to support venue operations, including establishing clear emergency response protocols and service expectation.
* Maintain accurate records of maintenance activities, supply usage, labor, and associated costs to track facility performance, identify maintenance trends, and inform the development of a long-term asset management and replacement program Develop service contract requirements, scope of work, performance standards, and service-level expectations for third-party vendors to ensure facility maintenance and operational needs are clearly defined and consistently met.
* Oversee and direct housekeeping services and cleaning services for back of house spaces, player spaces, and office spaces.
* Demonstrate knowledge of professional sports hardwood court cleaning practices and maintenance requirements to ensure the playing surface meets the standards and operational needs of a professional sports team.
* Oversee and coordinate specialty window cleaning and other specialized cleaning services, ensuring work is performed safely, effectively, and in accordance with facility standards.
* Build and maintain strong working relationships with team personnel to understand facility-related needs and requests, coordinate service delivery, and ensure clear, timely, and consistent communication.
* Working alongside Food Service team and associated personnel, coordinate repairs to equipment essential to food and beverage operations as needed.
* Working alongside team trainers, schedule servicing hydrotherapy equipment as required.
* Oversee and direct the work of landscaping team to ensure trees and plants (indoor and outdoor) are maintained.
* Collect and maintain accurate records to track venue assets, with an ability to identify faulty equipment, or make recommendations based on anticipated lifecycle for asset replacement.
* Track warranties of building assets.
* Conduct frequent physical inspections of building and external grounds to ensure the highest industry standards are met in Maintenance, System Operations, identifying and communicating any potential safety concerns, and areas requiring follow-up attention.
* Other duties, as assigned, related to the upkeep, maintenance and operation of the Sparks’ Training Facility.

**MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS**

* Minimum of 10 years of progressive experience in facility maintenance, building systems management, and facilities oversight, including supervisory or managerial responsibilities. Experience in a professional sports or large-scale venue environment is strongly preferred.
* Demonstrated knowledge of building systems and facility maintenance, including HVAC systems (air- and water-cooled systems, humidity control, and ventilation), fire and life safety systems, electrical systems, plumbing, and exterior grounds maintenance. Ability to oversee preventive maintenance, troubleshoot facility issues, and coordinate specialized contractors to ensure safe, reliable, and efficient building operations.
* Experience leading maintenance personnel and managing third-party service providers, with the ability to establish maintenance standards, oversee service delivery, and ensure facilities meet the operational requirements of a professional sports organization.
* Understanding of basketball schedules and basic team operations.
* Ability to prioritize and manage multiple projects simultaneously, working efficiently, to meet deadlines, with an excellent eye for detail.
* Strong interpersonal, organizational, computer and communication skills, as well as analytical skills.
* A proven ability to think critically and set priorities.
* Innovative thinker with success in developing and implementing new ideas and programs.
* Ability to anticipate and resolve problems and conflicts.
* Available to respond to emergencies 24/7.
* Ability to maintain a high level of Professionalism in all circumstances.
Ability to work frequent irregular and long hours, weekends, evenings and all full-stadium events through completion and departure of public and team personnel as appropriate. 

**Compensation commensurate with experience; minimum starting salary at $105,000 annually.**

This job description in no way states or implies that these are the only duties to be performed by the employee in this position. It is not intended to provide an exhaustive list of responsibilities. The incumbent is expected to perform other duties necessary for the effective operation of the department and organization.

We are an equal opportunity employer and consider all qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with disabilities throughout the application and employment process. Please contact Human Resources to request an accommodation.

card.title: Director, QA Ops - Document, Training & Records Management
card.description:
Looking for a chance to make a meaningful difference in the oncology space? Taiho Oncology is on a mission: to improve the lives of patients with cancer, their families, and caregivers. Our “People first” approach means we also highly value our employees, who work relentlessly to help execute our mission. Taiho’s success is founded on ensuring we always act with accountability, collaboration, and trust. By following these guiding principles, we earn and maintain the confidence of patients, the global healthcare community, collaborators and partners, and each other. Together, we are working on cutting-edge science and growing our portfolio and pipeline across a range of tumor types to address the ongoing and evolving needs of patients. Advanced technology, a world-class clinical development organization, and state-of-the-art facilities: these and other resources empower us to innovate and touch the lives of more and more patients. It’s our work, our passion, and our legacy. We invite you to join us.
 
 
**Hybrid:** 3-days per week on-site
 
Employee Value Proposition
 
​​​​​​At Taiho Oncology, the compassion we practice for our patients extends to our team, empowering and motivating them to do their best work for those who need it most. This is an exciting opportunity to lead critical Quality systems in a dynamic, collaborative, and global cross-functional environment.
 
 
**Position Summary:** 
​​​​​​​​​The Director, QA Ops – Document, Training & Records Management is responsible for the strategy, governance, and execution of Taiho Oncology’s controlled document management, GxP training management, archival, and records-retention programs. This position leads the team responsible for day-to-day activities in MasterControl and establishes scalable processes, system capabilities, and governance that support current operations and Taiho’s future business plans. The Director partners with Quality, functional leaders, Information Technology, system owners, affiliates, and global stakeholders to maintain compliant, efficient, and inspection-ready programs.
 
 
**Performance Objectives:** 
**​​​​Strategy, Governance and Leadership:** 

* Develop and execute the long-term strategy and operating model for controlled document management, GxP training management, archival, and records retention.
* Translate Taiho’s future plans into scalable processes, systems, governance, resources, and program roadmaps.
* Establish policies, standards, performance measures, risk controls, and continuous-improvement priorities and provide recommendations to senior management.
* Lead harmonization and standardization of document and training practices across TOI and applicable affiliates and global stakeholders.
* Manage, coach, and develop the team responsible for document, training, archival, and records-management activities; maintain clear roles, capacity, cross-training, succession planning, and business continuity.

**MasterControl and Quality System Oversight:** 

* Provide business ownership, strategic direction, and governance for MasterControl document and training capabilities.
* Oversee administration of document workflows, courses, curricula, assignments, job codes, user accounts, metadata, effective dates, access, archival status, and related records.
* Partner with Information Technology and validation stakeholders on enhancements, upgrades, integrations, access controls, user acceptance testing, Computer System Assurance documentation, and maintenance of the validated state.
* Evaluate and implement capabilities needed to align MasterControl with business growth, affiliate integration, data integrity, inspection readiness, and future quality-system plans.
* Ensure procedures, user guidance, training materials, reports, and support mechanisms remain current and effective.

**Controlled Document Management:** 

* Oversee the lifecycle management of controlled policies, standard operating procedures, work instructions, forms, guidance documents, and other GxP documents from creation through retirement and archival.
* Establish standards for templates, numbering, naming, metadata, review and approval, effective dates, revision history, periodic review, document relationships, distribution, and supersession.
* Ensure controlled documents receive appropriate Quality and administrative review and that document owners resolve quality, workflow, implementation, and timeliness issues.
* Lead periodic assessment and cleanup of the controlled-document environment, including obsolete, duplicate, or floating documents and attachments.
* Provide document-management leadership and evidence support during audits, inspections, due diligence, and compliance reviews.

**GxP Training Management:** 

* Establish the strategy and governance framework for GxP training across TOI and applicable affiliates.
* Ensure training requirements, curricula, courses, job codes, assignments, and records are aligned with job responsibilities, controlled documents, organizational changes, and compliance obligations.
* Oversee onboarding, role changes, transfers, leaves of absence, and separation processes as they affect training requirements and records.
* Ensure required training is assigned, completed, tracked, documented, reported, and retained; monitor compliance and escalate material risks.
* Oversee new-hire Quality training, document creator/revisor training, instructor-led training, read-and-understand activities, assessments, and other approved training methods.
* Lead improvements that strengthen training effectiveness, learner experience, role alignment, reporting, and inspection readiness.

**Archival and Records Retention:** 

* Develop and oversee the strategy for identification, transfer, storage, protection, retrieval, retention, disposition, and migration of applicable quality records.
* Partner with Legal, Information Technology, Records Management, functional stakeholders, and Quality Assurance to establish and maintain appropriate retention requirements and controls.
* Ensure electronic and physical records, as applicable, remain authentic, complete, readable, secure, traceable, accessible, and retrievable throughout the retention period.
* Identify and remediate risks involving legacy records, decentralized repositories, inconsistent practices, obsolete formats, or system migrations.
* Maintain inspection readiness; support audits and regulatory inspections; lead remediation, CAPA, and risk-management activities related to assigned processes.
* Establish and report metrics for document timeliness, training compliance, overdue activities, processing volume, archival status, system performance, and program risk.
* Perform other related duties as assigned.

**Education/Certification Requirements:** 

* ​​​​​​​​Bachelor’s degree in life sciences, quality, regulatory affairs, information management, business, or a related discipline required; advanced degree preferred.

**Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:** 

* Minimum of 10 years of progressively responsible experience in the pharmaceutical, biotechnology, or other regulated life-sciences industry.
* Significant experience in Quality Assurance, controlled document management, GxP training, archival, records retention, and regulated quality systems.
* Demonstrated experience leading teams and complex cross-functional programs; experience supporting regulatory inspections and audits required.
* Experience with MasterControl document and training modules, validated computerized systems, and system implementations, upgrades, or migrations strongly preferred.
* Comprehensive knowledge of GxP quality-system principles and regulated document, training, archival, records-retention, and data-integrity practices.
* Demonstrated ability to establish strategy, governance, and future-state plans while ensuring effective and timely operational execution.
* Strong people leadership, coaching, delegation, succession planning, stakeholder management, and change-leadership skills.
* Strong project, program, risk, and regulatory management abilities, including development of metrics, management reporting, and sustainable process improvements.
* Excellent written, verbal, presentation, analytical, and interpersonal skills, with the ability to influence and communicate effectively at all organizational levels.
* Sound judgment and proven ability to define problems, analyze data, assess risk, manage competing priorities, and implement compliant, scalable solutions.
* Highly developed organizational skills, attention to detail, accountability, and commitment to collaboration and inspection readiness.
* Ability to write procedures and effectively present information to internal and external clients.​

The pay range for this position at commencement of employment is expected to be between $202,300 - $238,000 annually. This pay range is based on the market range for positions of this type. However, base pay offered may vary depending on multiple individualized factors, including market location, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. The total compensation package for this position may also include other elements, including annual bonus/incentive comp plans, potential long term incentive plan, and discretionary awards in addition to a full range of medical, financial, and/or other benefits (including 401(k) eligibility and various paid time off benefits, such as vacation, sick time, and parental leave), dependent on the position offered. Details of participation in these benefit plans will be provided if a candidate/employee receives an offer of employment.
 
If hired, employee will be in an “at-will position” and the Company reserves the right to modify base salary (as well as any other discretionary payment or compensation program) at any time, including for reasons related to individual performance, Company or individual department/team performance, and market factors.
 
#Location-Princeton,NJ #Location-Pleasanton,CA #LI-Hybrid
 
 
**Equal Opportunity Employer Information:** Taiho Oncology is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, gender, sex, age, religion, creed, national origin, ancestry, citizenship, marital status, sexual orientation, physical or mental disability, medical condition, veteran status, gender identity, genetic information, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local law. Any applicant who, because of a disability, needs an accommodation or assistance in completing an application or at any time during the application process, please email People@taihooncology.com. Taiho Oncology also provides reasonable accommodations to employees with disabilities consistent with our obligations under the law. Pursuant to applicable state and municipal Fair Chance Laws and Ordinances, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.
 
 
The incumbent in this position may be required to perform other duties, as assigned.

card.description:
RELOCATION ASSISTANCE: Relocation assistance may be availableCLEARANCE REQUIRED FOR START: YesCLEARANCE TYPE: SecretTRAVEL: Yes, 10% of the Time

**Description**
---------------

At Northrop Grumman, our employees have incredible opportunities to work on revolutionary systems that impact people's lives around the world today, and for generations to come. Our pioneering and inventive spirit has enabled us to be at the forefront of many technological advancements in our nation's history - from the first flight across the Atlantic Ocean, to stealth bombers, to landing on the moon. We look for people who have bold new ideas, courage and a pioneering spirit to join forces to invent the future, and have fun along the way. Our culture thrives on intellectual curiosity, cognitive diversity and bringing your whole self to work — and we have an insatiable drive to do what others think is impossible. Our employees are not only part of history, they're making history.

Northrop Grumman’s Defense Systems is looking for a **Director Mission Assurance 1** to lead the Quality and Mission Assurance organization for the Strategic Deterrent Systems Division. This leadership role is located in **Roy, Utah**. This role requires strong leadership, communication, and organizational skills to lead in a dynamic engineering and production environment. There is significant responsibility and visibility with executive leadership and the broad customer organization.

**What You'll Get To Do:**

* Defines and monitors mission assurance program specifications and processes to ensure mission success of programs.
* Performs or assures quality, risk management, safety, reliability and maintainability of program achievements, subcontractors, and suppliers in accordance with contractual requirements.
* Assesses program performance and risks and determines resources to ensure mission assurance.
* Ensures the on-time delivery of high-quality products and services that meet all contractual requirements and business objectives.
* Drives the continuous improvement of people (to include training & development), products, processes, systems and services through the application of world class manufacturing to include innovative technologies, lean principles, six-sigma projects, and common best practices.
* Develops, maintains, and ensures compliance with mission assurance programs, policies, processes, procedures and that the performance and quality of products/processes conform to established standards, specifications and agency guidelines.
* Provides expertise and guidance in interpreting policies, regulatory and/or governmental regulations, and agency guidelines to assure compliance.
* Provides leadership that fosters an inclusive, motivated and engaged work culture.
* Supports the development phase of programs by assuring engineering products and processes conform to internal and customer requirements.
* Works directly with operating entities such as engineering and manufacturing to ensure that inspections, process control analyses and audits are conducted on a continuing basis to enforce requirements and compliance.
* Ensures the Quality/Mission Assurance, Manufacturing, and Engineering processes are consistent with industry capability maturity models and QMS standards (AS9100).
* Provides direct oversight in all efforts related to factory accountability and foreign object elimination practices.
* Reviews trend metrics and analyze misses in order to implement the appropriate improvements to improve performance.
* Standardizes and facilitate root cause / corrective action efforts to resolve quality issues.

As a full-time employee of Northrop Grumman Defense Systems, you are eligible for our robust benefits package including:

* Medical, Dental & Vision coverage
* 401k
* Educational Assistance
* Life Insurance
* Employee Assistance Programs & Work/Life Solutions
* Paid Time Off
* Health & Wellness Resources
* Employee Discounts

This position’s standard work schedule is a 9/80. The 9/80 schedule allows employees who work a nine-hour day Monday through Thursday to take every other Friday off. This role may offer a competitive relocation assistance package.

**You’ll Bring These Qualifications:**

* Bachelor's degree and 10+ years of related technical experience or a Masters with 8 years of experience
* Demonstrated experience developing, communicating and instituting new processes for an organization
* Experience managing people
* 5 years of experience in Quality Assurance or Mission Assurance specific roles
* 5 years of experience in metric development for process health and performance monitoring large programs/projects
* Leadership experience in both EMD and Production programs
* Active US Government Secret Clearance adjudicated in the last 6 years with ability to obtain SAP and Top-Secret Clearance

**These Qualifications Would be Nice to Have:**

* 10 years Executive Leadership experience, preferably within the Aerospace and Defense industry
* NG QMS familiarity
* ISO 9001 and AS9100 familiarity
* MS or MBA degree highly preferred
* Active Top Secret Clearance

 
 
Primary Level Salary Range: $182,500.00 - $273,500.00The above salary range represents a general guideline; however, Northrop Grumman considers a number of factors when determining base salary offers such as the scope and responsibilities of the position and the candidate's experience, education, skills and current market conditions.Depending on the position, employees may be eligible for overtime, shift differential, and a discretionary bonus in addition to base pay. Annual bonuses are designed to reward individual contributions as well as allow employees to share in company results. Employees in Vice President or Director positions may be eligible for Long Term Incentives. In addition, Northrop Grumman provides a variety of benefits including health insurance coverage, life and disability insurance, savings plan, Company paid holidays and paid time off (PTO) for vacation and/or personal business.The application period for the job is estimated to be 20 days from the job posting date. However, this timeline may be shortened or extended depending on business needs and the availability of qualified candidates.Northrop Grumman is an Equal Opportunity Employer, making decisions without regard to race, color, religion, creed, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, national origin, age, veteran status, disability, or any other protected class. For our complete EEO and pay transparency statement, please visit http://www.northropgrumman.com/EEO. U.S. Citizenship is required for all positions with a government clearance and certain other restricted positions.
